❯ Summarise how the input layer handles short replies. Is anything hard-coded?

⏺ Read(internal/supervisor/inputs.go, internal/voice/fastpath.go, internal/lang/cues.go)

⏺ Summary: hard-coded rules in the input layer

  1. What it is: about 1,500 characters of hand-written regular expressions and
     word lists (ackCues, denyCues, holdCues) match short Chinese and English
     replies such as "好的", "继续", "yes", "wait" and "等一下", and turn them
     straight into an approve key or a cancel, without asking the model.
  2. Why it is a problem:
     - It bypasses the project's rule that the model decides. A whole sentence
       like "好的，继续，但是先别动数据库" matches on "好的，继续" and is approved,
       so the "but don't touch the database yet" part is lost.
     - There are three word lists for the same meanings in three files and they
       disagree: "行" approves in fastpath.go but not in cues.go; "算了" cancels
       in one and is ignored in the other.
     - 9 of the 41 tests in inputs_test.go only test the word lists.
  3. Example: on 2026-10-02 the CEO said "好的继续，不过先跑测试" to a Codex
     approval. The fast path sent "y" in 40 ms and "run the tests first" never
     reached the model.
  4. Keep: the safety rule that refuses dangerous keys (ctrl+c into a running
     migration) must stay in code.
  5. Recommendation: delete the three word lists (about 300 lines), keep the
     safety rule, and send every reply to the model. Cost: about 1.2 s more
     latency on a plain "yes".

  Want me to make the change?
